Metadata.title: OdyssAI : The AI-narrated multiverse
Metadata.description: A multiverse narrative game: your own universe, narrated by an AI, linked to other players’ worlds through a shared General Lore.

Hero.title: Build any world you want. Then go and visit everyone else's.
Hero.description: Every player shapes their own world, guided by an AI narrator. Universes cross paths, trade characters and events, and share one common General Lore. The AI tells the story, the engine decides what is true.

faq.question: What exactly is a credit?
faq.answer: One action. A game turn costs one, a message to your character during its creation costs one too, and bringing a world to life costs twenty-five. The scale is the same for everyone and does not depend on how much the narrator writes.

faq.question: Why does a world cost twenty-five credits?
faq.answer: Because it takes at least seven passes to write: a charter, a lore, factions, a political order, characters, their ties, then a check that reads it all back and may ask for a rewrite. It is the most expensive move in the game, and the only one you make once.

faq.question: Do my credits roll over?
faq.answer: On a subscription, no: every month your reserve goes back to your tier's grant, no more and no less, otherwise six months away would buy six months ahead. On the Rider tier, which grants nothing monthly, the question does not arise: whatever you have not spent stays as long as your account does.

faq.question: What happens when I run out?
faq.answer: Your worlds stay, your games too. You simply cannot play a turn until the renewal, or until you move up a tier.

faq.question: What is the first-hundred bonus?
faq.answer: The first hundred sign-ups get thirty credits on top of their starting reserve, once, without asking. It is not a tier you pick: it is a bonus added to the account, and it shows in the ledger like any other grant.

faq.question: Where is my subscription handled?
faq.answer: At Stripe, never here: no card details are ever entered on OdyssAI. Cancelling goes through the same portal, and your tier stays active until the end of the period you already paid for.

Concept.metaDescription: An online narrative role-playing game led by an AI narrator that remembers everything. Your choices have consequences that last.
Concept.lead: You invent a world. You live your story in it. Then you go and live everyone else's.
intro: OdyssAI is a narrative role-playing game you play online. The game master is an AI narrator: it describes places, speaks for the characters, adjudicates your actions and remembers everything that happened. No need to gather a group on a Friday night, or to find someone willing to run the session. The narrator is always there, and it knows your story.

sections.title: You are the hero
body: The narrator offers you choices, but you are never bound by them. You can write what your character does, in your own words, and the world reacts. When the outcome is uncertain, you roll a d20. Chance stays part of the game, just as it does around a real table.
Your decisions have consequences that last. A character you betrayed will remember it three sessions later. A door you left open stays open.

sections.title: You build your world
body: Fantasy, space opera, cyberpunk, horror, or something that has no name yet. One sentence is enough to start: a place, an era, one strange rule. The narrator builds the rest with you, and you keep the final say on everything.

sections.title: You travel
body: Every world created on OdyssAI belongs to the same multiverse. Your character can cross the rifts that link them and go live an adventure in another player's world. They remain themselves, with their temperament and their memories, but they find a role there that makes sense.

sections.title: Nothing stands alone
body: Worlds intersect. You may come across the traces of another traveller: a letter, a rumour, a place they changed before you passed through. You can also meet them. And what truly matters eventually joins the General Lore, the history shared by every world.

sections.title: Who it is for
body: For roleplayers who do not always have a table. For those who have carried a world in their head for years and want to finally see it live. For the curious who want a story where their choices count.

Universes.metaDescription: Create your world, its charter and its laws. You remain its creator: the narrator plays in it, it never decides in your stead what is true.
intro: On OdyssAI, every player can create their own universe: a world with its places, its peoples, its history and its laws. You are its creator and its keeper. The narrator plays in it, brings it to life and expands it with you, but it never decides in your stead what is true in your world.

sections.title: Start with one sentence
body: “An archipelago where the tide never goes back out.” “A space station whose owner nobody knows.” You start from there, and the narrator offers you a geography, factions, tensions, secrets. You keep, you change, you discard. You can define everything in detail before playing, or let the world reveal itself session after session.

sections.title: The world charter
body: Every universe has a charter. It is its DNA: what exists and what does not (eg. magic, technology, gods), the tone, the rules that are not up for debate, what is off limits, the content rating. Is death permanent? Can machines dream? You decide. The narrator upholds the charter in all circumstances, including when facing travellers from elsewhere.

sections.title: A world that remembers
body: Every character met, every place visited, every notable event is written into your world's canon. Its inhabitants remember what happened. The more you play, the denser, the more coherent and the more inhabited your world becomes.

sections.title: Opening your doors
body: Your world can stay closed, open by invitation, or welcome every traveller in the multiverse. You choose how they arrive: as inhabitants who have always lived there, as strangers fallen through a rift, or as mere passing echoes. You also set how far they are allowed to change things.
After each visit you receive the travellers' chronicle: what they did, who they met, what moved. You decide what becomes canon. Your world stays yours.

sections.title: An identity
body: Every world has its colour, which tints the whole interface once you step inside, and its constellation on the map of the multiverse. You know where you are at first glance.

Multiverse.metaDescription: Your character crosses the rifts and keeps their essence. You choose what they do, the world's creator decides what it changes.
Multiverse.lead: Your character travels. They remain themselves.
intro: Every world on OdyssAI forms a single multiverse. Rifts open between them, and your character can cross.

One rule holds all the rest together: you choose what your character does, the world's creator decides what it changes. Nobody takes control of another player's world, or of another player's character.

sections.title: What crosses over, what stays behind
body: Your character carries their essence: their name, their temperament, what drives them forward, their flaw, their memories. Everything else belongs to the world they leave behind: their trade, their appearance, their skills, their belongings, their reputation.
On arrival, the narrator translates that essence into the reality of the new world. You see the proposal before you enter, and you can adjust it.

sections.title: The same, differently
body: Ilse is a cartographer in les Terres de Vasse, obsessed with places that appear on no map. Crossing the rift to Station Hélione, she becomes a navigator and plots routes away from the official beacons. In Ville-Basse 2099, she maps the underground networks for whoever pays her. In le Marais d'Ossian, she draws paths that shift at night.
Four roles with nothing in common. And yet it is her every time.

sections.title: Three ways to arrive
body: Depending on what the world accepts, you enter as a native, a traveller or an echo.

As a native, the world absorbs you: you have always lived there, and only a few blurred memories betray your origin. As a traveller, you arrive a stranger, aware of where you come from, and the inhabitants can feel it. As an echo, you are only a passing projection: you cannot die, but your influence stays light.

sections.title: Crossing paths with others
body: Encounters often begin with traces. A letter signed with an unknown name, an innkeeper who mentions a stranger carrying odd maps, a place another traveller transformed before you. Then comes the day you are both in the same scene. Each of you keeps control of your own character; the narrator plays the world and adjudicates what happens between you.

sections.title: What you bring back
body: You do not come back with a sword from another world. You come back with memories, and sometimes a mark: a scar, a new fear, a conviction. What you live elsewhere changes who your character is, not what they own. That is how each world stays balanced, and how every journey counts.

Lore.metaDescription: The Fixed Star, the rifts, the great arcs: the truths shared by every world in OdyssAI.
Lore.lead: What every world has in common.
intro: Every world has its own history. The General Lore is the one that links them: the few truths that hold everywhere, and the events large enough to have marked several worlds at once.

sections.title: The Fixed Star
body: In every world, whatever its nature, one star shines in the same place in the sky. The sailors of Vasse use it to find their way back to port. The pilots of Hélione long mistook it for a beacon. In Ville-Basse it is only visible on blackout nights, and on those nights people come out into the street to look at it.
Nobody knows what it is. All anyone knows is that it is the same everywhere.

sections.title: The rifts
body: Where the veil between two worlds wears thin, a rift opens. Some are stable and known, guarded, sometimes worshipped. Others open one night and close again the next day. Nobody knows who opened them the first time, or whether anyone controls them.

sections.title: The travellers
body: Those who pass from one world to another carry different names depending on where they land. In some worlds they are welcomed as messengers. In others they are feared, or hunted. Each creator decides how their world looks upon travellers.

sections.title: How a story becomes legend
body: It all starts in one world. What happens there becomes canon when its creator validates it. When an event touches several worlds, when it has been lived by several travellers or when it changes the nature of the rifts, it can enter the General Lore. It then becomes a truth for the whole multiverse, and each world interprets it its own way.
Your world can become a legend elsewhere. One day, in a world you have never visited, someone will speak of the archipelago where the tide never goes back out.

sections.title: The great arcs
body: Every now and then, something happens to all the worlds at once. The Star wavers. The rifts multiply. Each world lives the event according to its own logic, and every player can influence its outcome. These are the great arcs of the multiverse, and they are what writes the General Lore.

About.metaDescription: Who makes OdyssAI, why, and where the project stands: a closed alpha for a hundred players, built by an independent engineer.
About.lead: A game made by one person, not a studio. Here is who, why, and where things stand.
intro: OdyssAI is designed and built by Joachim Alexandre Jasmin, an independent software engineer, alone. No team, no funding round, no roadmap imposed from outside.

sections.title: Who makes OdyssAI
body: Joachim Alexandre Jasmin is an independent software engineer. His daily work covers full-stack development, infrastructure and applied AI, and he teaches those subjects to beginners and experienced developers alike.
OdyssAI is a personal project. He writes the code, the texts and the infrastructure, and he answers the messages sent from the Contact page himself.
The site's publisher, legal status and contact details are in the legal notice.

sections.title: Why this game
body: Role-playing needs a table, a game master, and an evening when everyone is free. Plenty of people have carried a world in their head for years without ever lining up those three things.

OdyssAI starts there: a game master always available, a world that belongs to you, and sessions that remember what you did. The multiverse comes next, when your character crosses a rift and goes to live in someone else's world.

sections.title: How it is built
body: Three principles guide the code, and they show in the pages of this site.
The model tells, the code decides. No state change comes from the generated text: a story claiming the opposite of a rule does not change it.
Your world owes nothing to anyone. The works you cite as inspiration serve to extract themes, and three independent checks keep a borrowed name from surviving into the generated world.
What you write is yours. You can erase your account and your worlds whenever you want, and whatever would be kept is described on the Privacy page.

sections.title: Where the project stands
body: OdyssAI is in closed alpha, limited to a hundred spots. The game isn't live yet: signing up reserves a spot and the thirty credits that come with it, and the invite goes out when it opens. The banner at the top of the site says where sign-ups stand.
An alpha is unstable by nature: features change, others disappear, and a technical change can lose a universe. That is the price of coming in early, and it is stated in the terms and conditions.
There is no release date. It would be made up.

sections.title: Writing to us
body: The Contact page sends a message straight through, with or without an account. A question, a bug, an idea, a request about your data: everything is read.

intro: These terms govern the use of OdyssAI and the sale of the subscriptions attached to it. They apply from the moment an account is created.
OdyssAI is published by Joachim Alexandre Jasmin, sole trader, whose details appear in the legal notice.

sections.title: Purpose
body: OdyssAI is an online narrative role-playing game whose game master is a language model. The service covers creating universes, running sessions, and the features around them.
Creating an account means accepting these terms. Anyone who does not accept them should not create an account.

sections.title: Access during the alpha
body: The service is in closed alpha, limited to one hundred players. Beyond that, registration is refused until a wider opening.

An alpha is unstable by nature: features may change, be removed, or stop working without notice. Universes and sessions may be lost during a technical change. Do not entrust anything to it you could not bear to lose.
Access may be suspended for maintenance, without compensation.

sections.title: Account and identity
body: Identity is handled by a Keycloak server we administer. Email address, password and two-factor authentication live there; the game profile lives in the application database.
An account is personal. You are responsible for what is done with yours, and must report any use you did not authorise.
The service is reserved for people aged fifteen and over.

sections.title: What the narrator writes
body: The narrator's text is produced by a language model. It may be inaccurate, inconsistent, or upsetting despite the safeguards in place. It is neither advice nor reference information, and we accept no liability for its content.
Game state is decided by code, never by the generated text: a story that claims something contrary to the rules does not make it true in the session.
No generated answer is cached to be served again to someone else.

sections.title: What you write
body: You keep ownership of the text you write and the universes you create. You grant us only the licence needed to run the service: to store, display, transmit to the models, and show to other players when you open your world.

You warrant that you have the right to write what you write. You must not reproduce someone else's work: the titles you cite as inspiration serve to extract themes, and the resulting world must borrow nothing from them.
What the model writes from your input is not guaranteed to be original or protectable, the law on automated output remaining unsettled.

sections.title: Conduct and moderation
body: Unlawful, hateful, sexual content involving minors, content inciting violence or harassment, and attempts to bypass the service's safeguards are all forbidden.
Everything a player writes passes through two moderation layers, one lexical and one classifier. A rejected message is not passed to the narrator.
A breach may lead to suspension or closure of the account, with no refund of credits already spent.

sections.title: Credits
body: Play is consumed in credits. A game turn costs one, a character-creation message one, and generating a world twenty-five. The scale is published on the pricing page and may change; a change never applies retroactively to credits already spent.
Credits have no monetary value, cannot be resold, cannot be transferred between accounts, and are not refundable in cash.

On a subscription, the reserve returns to the tier's grant each period and does not roll over. On the free tier, which grants nothing monthly, whatever you have not spent stays as long as the account exists.
Moderation and the narrator's memory are never charged.

sections.title: Subscriptions, prices and payment
body: Tiers and their prices appear on the pricing page. Prices are in euros, inclusive of tax where applicable.
Payment is handled by Stripe Payments Europe. No card details are entered or stored on OdyssAI. Subscribing and managing go through pages hosted by Stripe.
The subscription is monthly and renews automatically until cancelled. The credit grant is issued on each confirmed payment.
A price change applies only from the next renewal and is announced beforehand.

sections.title: Cancellation
body: You may cancel at any time from the Stripe portal, reachable from your account. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the period already paid for: your tier stays active until then.
After cancellation, remaining credits are kept and can still be spent; no new grant is issued.
Deleting your account cancels the subscription immediately, with no refund of the current period.
We may cancel a subscription for a breach of these terms or if the service shuts down, with a pro-rata refund of the unused period in the latter case.

sections.title: Right of withdrawal
body: You have fourteen days to withdraw from a subscription, under article L221-18 of the French consumer code.

By requesting immediate access to the service, you agree that performance begins before the end of that period and waive your right of withdrawal, as provided by article L221-28 of the same code. This waiver is requested at the time of payment.
As long as you have spent no credit from the period subscribed, we refund it on request.

sections.title: Personal data
body: Data processing is described on the Privacy page, which forms part of these terms.
You can erase your game account from your personal space. Identity itself is deleted from your account console, the identity server remaining the source.

sections.title: Liability
body: The service is provided as is, with no guarantee of continuous availability or freedom from error, which is the nature of an alpha.
Our liability cannot exceed the amounts you actually paid over the last twelve months, excluding personal injury or gross negligence, which the law excludes from any limitation.
No clause deprives a consumer of the rights the law grants them.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
body: These terms may change. A substantial change is announced on the site before taking effect, and for a subscriber, at the latest at their next renewal.
Continuing to use the service after it takes effect means accepting it. Otherwise, cancellation remains open at any time.

sections.title: Governing law and disputes
body: These terms are governed by French law.
In case of a dispute, an amicable solution is sought first: write to joachim.jasmin-dev@proton.me.
A consumer may use a consumer mediator free of charge, or refer the matter to the European online dispute resolution platform. Failing agreement, the French courts have jurisdiction.

Privacy.metaDescription: What OdyssAI collects, why, for how long, and how to exercise your rights.
Privacy.lead: What we know about you, why, and how to take it back.
intro: OdyssAI collects the bare minimum needed to open an account and to tell you when the alpha opens. Nothing is sold, nothing is passed on for advertising.

sections.title: Data controller
body: Joachim Alexandre Jasmin, details in the legal notice. For any request: joachim.jasmin-dev@proton.me.

sections.title: What is collected
body: When you create an account: your email address and the password you choose. The password is never readable, our identity server keeps only a hash of it, and it never passes through the application.
While using the service: an account identifier, the creation date and sign-in dates.
When the game opens: your universes, characters and progress. This policy will be extended before then.

sections.title: Why, and on what basis
body: To create and secure your account, and to sign you in. Legal basis: performing the pre-contractual steps you ask for by opening an account.
To tell you when the alpha opens and send news about the project. Legal basis: your consent, withdrawable at any time, every message carrying an unsubscribe link.
No advertising, no profiling, no resale.

sections.title: The site guide
body: The home page offers a guide that answers questions about the game. Every question asked is recorded for thirty days, to measure how the service is used and to spot the questions that keep coming back. That record holds neither your IP address nor your account identifier: nothing ties it to you.

A question that finds no answer in the guide's FAQ is passed to a language model provider, through OpenRouter, to be answered. The service is configured to accept only providers that do not retain the exchanges.

A sample of the exchanges leaves a technical trace with LangSmith, on its European infrastructure, to monitor the service. Those traces hold neither your question nor the answer: only counters, timings and the model name. The guide needs no personal data to answer: do not put any in your questions.

sections.title: How long
body: Account data is kept for as long as the account exists. Deleting it from the My account page is immediate: there is no delay and no restore.
Questions asked to the guide are erased after thirty days.
Server technical logs are kept for at most twelve months.

A world other players have already visited is not deleted with its author: it is kept, detached from them, and emptied of everything they typed, namely the works they named, their free description and the creation conversation. What remains is the text written by the model, with no link to a person.
Likewise, a character other players met stays in their stories, described as dead. Its name is the only thing that remains of it.

sections.title: Who has access
body: Nobody but the publisher. The technical services are self-hosted on the project's server: the identity server, the mail server and the database.

Two providers are involved in the infrastructure: OVH SAS for hosting, in France, and Cloudflare, Inc. for delivery and network protection. Cloudflare is a US company; any transfers are covered by the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.

The guide relies on two further providers: OpenRouter, Inc. for access to language models, and LangChain, Inc. for LangSmith technical traces, on its European infrastructure. Both are US companies, covered by the same standard contractual clauses.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You have rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability. Erasure is done straight from the My account page, without having to ask. For the other rights, write to the contact address; you will get an answer within one month.
If it does not satisfy you, you may lodge a complaint with the French authority CNIL, 3 place de Fontenoy, 75007 Paris, at cnil.fr.

Deleting your account here erases your game data. Your email address and password live at the identity service, where the confirmation screen takes you to delete them yourself: we are not allowed to touch them on your behalf.

Cookies.metaDescription: The cookies OdyssAI sets, what they do, and why no consent is asked for today.
intro: OdyssAI currently sets only strictly necessary cookies. No analytics, no ad network, no social button.

sections.title: What is set
body: A language preference, remembering your choice between French and English. Kept for one year.
A session identifier, set when you sign in. It is opaque: it holds no data about you, only a reference the server knows how to read. It disappears when you sign out.
Our identity server's cookies, on the sso subdomain, for the duration of the sign-in and the session.
A guide cookie, set when you ask your first question and valid for one hour. Like the session one it is opaque, and it allows only a limited number of questions.
The cookies of Cloudflare's Turnstile anti-abuse service. It is loaded only when you send a question to the guide, never when the page opens, and checks that the request does not come from a bot.

sections.title: Your choice
body: A banner asks for your choice on your first visit. No analytics cookie is set before you answer, and declining costs you nothing.
Your choice is kept for six months in a cookie, then asked again. You can change it at any time through the “Manage cookies” link at the foot of every page.

The technical cookies listed above are not covered by that choice: article 82 of the French Data Protection Act exempts those strictly necessary to the requested service. Refusing them is done in your browser settings.

sections.title: Refusing them anyway
body: Your browser lets you block or clear cookies site by site. Blocking these will stop sign-in from working and make the site forget your language, but the rest stays readable.

CookieBanner.body: OdyssAI only sets technical cookies, needed for sign-in and for your language. You can refuse any future analytics right now.

Sheet.title: Character sheet
Sheet.lead: What the game actually holds of your character: attributes, talents, what they carry.

Sheet.notReady: Your world isn't ready yet: your sheet opens with it.
Sheet.standingHint: The narrator knows where it goes. You play it.
Sheet.freeHint: The arc is closed. What follows is written as you go.
Sheet.attributesAside: One to five, three is the middle
Sheet.progressHint: An attribute rises through use: every settled roll counts, failures included. Failing is the most ordinary way to learn.
Sheet.inventoryHint: Names, with no numeric effect: the narrator tells them, the engine doesn't compute them.
Sheet.stateHint: A failed physical exchange costs points, and the die alone decides: the narrator can neither spare you nor finish you. Three turns without a blow give one back. Down means out of the fight, never dead.

Sheet.marksAside: You do not come back from a world with a sword. You come back changed.
